lines.text: Plan the whole trip before the robot moves, then follow the plan.
Last time, it asked for thirty meters per second, then crawled the last stretch.
You've seen this shape on the arm: speed up, cruise, slow down. Now it's in meters.
On a trip under about two meters, there's no room to cruise, so the plan is a triangle.
When you press the button, the plan starts from where the robot is, and how fast it's already moving.
Every loop, the clock moves forward, and the plan says where the robot should be, and how fast it should go.
The plan's speed does most of the driving. A small correction pulls the robot toward where it should be.
Try it. Shove the robot, and flip the correction gain between ten and three.
At ten, a few centimeters of drift turn into meters per second. That's the buzz shape. Three is calm.
The command ends when the plan's clock runs out, even if the robot is a little short. That ending is what makes it a step.
A command with an ending can go in a list, after anything else.
